usage.10: Popups, popovers, modals, the CV page
usage.full circle: Only naturally round things: the score ring, avatars

corner radius scale.note: Never 0px, never above 10px. No pill-shaped buttons or tags. The same radius for the same type of element everywhere.

card and divider line.note: Soft warm line. White cards on paper. Dividers only between list rows, not around everything.

input and outlined button line.note: About 4.3:1 on white. The soft hairline (about 1.3:1) is too faint to show where a field is.

color usage discipline.note: One accent color should visually dominate any given screen or moment — do not let green (success), amber (flagged), and navy (brand/authority) all compete for attention in the same view at equal visual weight. Pick the single most important signal per screen (e.g., the score ring is the one green moment on the results screen) and let everything else recede to muted/navy/ink.

spacing discipline.note: Use a strict, consistent spacing scale (e.g., 4/8/12/16/24/32/48px) rather than arbitrary values. Elements of the same type must share identical padding/margin — inconsistency here is highly visible even when everything else is correct, and is a primary driver of a design feeling 'not premium.'

depth.cards, panels, buttons: No shadow. Flat, with the line only.
depth.floating layers: One soft shadow only for popovers, dropdowns, modals and toasts. Modals also dim the page behind them.

hero gradient.description: Subtle single-hue depth gradient for the hero section only. Not a decorative multi-hue gradient.

score reveal glow.description: Faint radial glow in the verified-green tone, used only behind the score circle on scan completion.

phone sizes.note: Apply below the tablet breakpoint (under 640). Title, body and label sizes do not change.

text input.note: 16px minimum on phones so browsers do not zoom in when a field is tapped.

usage rules.lora: Big moments only: hero headline, section titles, the score number, About page headings. Never in buttons, labels, tables, forms or prices.
usage rules.inter: Everything else: UI, body, labels, tables, forms.
usage rules.currency: Prices and currency are always Inter. Lora has no Naira sign. Load Inter's latin-ext subset so the Naira sign renders.
usage rules.numbers: Use tabular (aligned) digits in Inter for prices, usage counts and tables.
usage rules.loading: Self-host fonts (e.g., next/font). Load only: Lora 700 (and 600 only if a screen needs it); Inter 400, 500, 600 and 700.

success key color.name: same as secondary — score-pass semantic color

warning key color.name: same as tertiary — flagged semantic color

paper (page background).name: Warm Paper
paper (page background).note: Page background. Cards sit on it in white (#FFFFFF). Pairs with the warm hairline #E3E0D6.

typography: see 'font' block above — display/headline use Lora, title/body/label use Inter
notes: Replaces the original indigo/violet/sky-blue key colors, which read as generic AI-SaaS default.
Secondary (green) and tertiary (amber) intentionally double as the 'passing score' and 'flagged issue' semantic colors, so the brand palette IS the product's grading language.

Two gradients only, both restrained and single-hue: a subtle hero background gradient, and a faint radial glow behind the score circle on scan completion. No multi-hue decorative gradients on cards or buttons.

Display typography (score numbers, hero headline, section titles) uses Lora, a serif with real character, to reinforce the 'official grading report' identity. All UI, body copy, and dense text uses Inter for legibility.

color meaning rules.navy: Brand and trust: headings, primary buttons (including Get PRO / upgrade), links.
color meaning rules.green: Only means strong, passed, success. Never decoration.
color meaning rules.amber: Only means flagged / needs attention. Never decoration.
color meaning rules.red: Only real errors (failed payment, unreadable file). Never used for a flagged line.
color meaning rules.locked: Locked or PRO-only items use a neutral grey-blue with a lock icon, never amber or green.
color meaning rules.one star color per screen: One accent dominates each screen (e.g., the green score ring on results). Everything else recedes to navy, ink and neutrals.
color meaning rules.amber text rule: Amber (#C7742A) scores only 3.3:1 on paper and white-on-amber 3.5:1, below the 4.5:1 needed for text. Use amber for icons, dots, underlines and light tints only. Text inside amber areas uses warning30 (#7E4A1B, about 5.9:1 on its tint). No white text on amber buttons.
color meaning rules.green text rule: Green text on tints uses success30 (#2B6E53), not success40, to stay above 4.5:1.
color meaning rules.never: No purple, indigo or violet anywhere.

spacing.note: Only these values. 4 is for tiny pairs only (icon and its label).
rules: Related things sit close, unrelated things sit far apart.
The same type of element always has identical padding.
Section gap: marketing 96 desktop / 64 phone; app screens 32 desktop / 24 phone.

max content width.marketing: 1120 wide, centered, for every marketing page (nav side padding 160, footer inner 1120)

layout.touch targets: At least 44 x 44 on phones for every button and tappable icon.

results screen desktop.CV panel: fills the rest; the CV page maxes at 760, centered

layout.results screen phone: Step by step: (1) score and the 4 categories as a list; (2) tap a category to open its detail as the next screen with a back arrow; (3) a 'View on CV' toggle at the top of the detail screen shows the highlighted CV.
layout.results screen tablet: Left rail collapses into a row of tabs; middle detail and CV panel sit side by side.

tablet.design: Not designed in Figma. Only desktop and phone are designed.
tablet.build: The developer builds a proper tablet layout from the desktop and phone designs, using the same tokens (colors, fonts, spacing, components, states), so the whole app is fully responsive at every width. Tablet is tested like the other two sizes.

icons.color: Ink or muted grey. Colored icons follow the color rules (green means strong, amber means flagged).

buttons.primary: Navy fill, white text. One per section. Full width on phones.
buttons.destructive: Red, used only on the final Delete confirm.
buttons.loading: Label changes (e.g., 'Creating your account...') and the button locks.

small.use: Top bar and inside cards, desktop only. Same styles as the 44px buttons.

inputs.label: Always above the field, never placeholder only.
inputs.error: Under the field, red, with an icon.

tags and chips.flagged: Amber tint, warning30 text, flag icon
tags and chips.strong: Green tint, success30 text, check icon
tags and chips.rule: Always an icon plus a word, never color alone.

cards.style: White, 8px corners, padding 24 (16 on phone). App screens use the 1px soft line. Money, account and marketing screens use no outline (white card on the paper background). Inputs, selected states and dashed upload zones always keep their outline.
cards.locked category: Blurred detail, lock tag, issue count still shown
cards.recommended plan: 2px navy outline. A label such as 'Most popular' only if true. No fake badges.

popups and menus.modal: Dims the page behind; closes with Esc, the X, or tapping outside.

banners.style: Full-width strip inside the app with an icon and one action
banners.used for: 24-hour grace banner, renewal cancelled, payment problems

toasts.use: Light confirmations only (e.g., Copied). Fade after 5 seconds. Errors never use a toast.

loading and empty.loading: Grey placeholder shapes in the layout, not a spinner alone.
loading and empty.empty: One line of text and one button.

score ring.arc color: Green at 75 and above, amber below 75. Never red (red is for errors). 75 is a starting point to tune with real score data.
score ring.glow: The faint green radial glow only appears behind a green (75+) ring on completion.

states.hover: Navy buttons go slightly darker (primary20). Text buttons underline. Cards get a slightly stronger line.
states.keyboard focus: 2px navy ring with a 2px gap; white ring on navy backgrounds. Always visible.
states.disabled: 40% faded, ignores taps, and a short note says why when not obvious.
states.selected: 2px navy outline on cards; light navy tint on menu rows.
states.loading: Buttons keep their size and show a small spinner with the new label. Pages use grey placeholder shapes.
states.touch: Nothing important works on hover only. Every hover feature has a tap equivalent.

motion.properties: Fade and slide only. No bouncing, wiggling or pulsing.
allowed in: How It Works reveal (once, not repeated)
CV highlight when a category opens
green check when a fix is approved
motion.reduced motion: When the user's device asks for reduced motion, all animation switches off and final values show immediately.
motion.honest waiting: The processing screen shows real stages (e.g., 'Reading your CV...', 'Scoring...'), never a fake percentage bar. After about 15 seconds a 'taking longer than usual' message appears.

locked content.blur: The blur on a locked category is a picture of placeholder text, not real text hidden by CSS.
locked content.security: Real content for locked parts is never sent to the browser. Locked categories return counts only (SRS).

voice and copy.voice: A sharp, honest friend who knows recruiting. Direct, kind, specific. Never a cheerleader, never harsh.
rules: Plain words: 'Fix this line', not 'Optimise your bullet'.
Errors say what happened, why, and what to do next. Never 'Oops!'. Never blame the user.
Buttons are verb plus object: 'Scan my CV', 'Get PRO'. Not 'Submit' or 'Continue'.
Money is always plain: 'Renews on 1 Dec at ₦4,000. Cancel anytime.'
No fake urgency or scarcity. Offers and counters appear only when true.
No big promises ('Get hired fast'). Say what the product actually does.
AI text is a draft: 'We only use facts from your CV or what you tell us.' Never 'guaranteed'.
Sentence case everywhere except product names.
No emojis and no em dashes in product text. Short sentences.

terms.ATS: Explain once where it first appears: 'the software employers use to filter CVs'.

voice and copy.cv or resume: Product text says 'CV'. Marketing page titles and search text also include 'resume' so US visitors can find the site.
voice and copy.spelling: British English in all user-facing text (organise, colour).

marketing site.note: Rules learned while designing G1 to G9, the waitlist and the coming-soon page. Desktop is designed in Figma. Phones are built responsive in code from these rules.
marketing site.frame: 1440 wide. Nav 64 tall. Content column 1120, centered.
marketing site.section rhythm: 48 top and bottom padding per section (96 between sections). Section title Lora Bold 32/40, then 8 to subline, then 32 to content.
marketing site.buttons and inputs: Buttons 48 tall and inputs 48 tall on marketing pages (44 in the app).
marketing site.accent: Navy only. Green only for strong or passed. Amber only for flagged or missing. Red only for delete and form errors. Ink is used for text only (not for buttons or backgrounds) until the post-MVP accent decision.
marketing site.FAQ dropdown: White card, rows split by 1px soft dividers. Question Inter Semi Bold 16, answer Inter 15 muted. Chevron (Lucide, 1.5px, navy) on the right: down when closed, up when open. First item open, the rest closed. Several can be open together.
marketing site.plans: Day Pass is the default selected plan on the homepage. The currency switch changes every price on the page. Prices are in Inter because Lora has no naira sign.
marketing site.how it works: One section: video poster on top (click to play, never autoplay), then equal-width step cards with centered text. No second separate video section.
marketing site.legal pages: Two columns: sticky "On this page" list 280 wide and a 720 text column, 120 apart. Section headings Inter Bold 22, body Inter 17 or 16 muted.
marketing site.forms: Label Inter Semi Bold 14 above the field. Error text red 13 below the field and a red outline on the field. A sent or joined state replaces the form with a green check and a short message.
marketing site.waitlist and coming soon: One waitlist table for both pages, with a source field.

logo.lockup: Component "Logo / Lockup": navy mark 28px, lowercase "gradea" Inter Bold 21 navy, gap 10.
logo.favicon: Use a simplified mark. A 16px version may need the notch removed.
logo.admin: The admin dashboard shows the logo with no extra word beside it.

social icons.where: Footer only, never in the nav. The coming-soon page and the About founder card also use them.
social icons.set: LinkedIn, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, X, Instagram (this order). First wave live: LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, X. Show an icon only when its link is filled.
social icons.styles: Light rounded squares (tint fill) on light backgrounds, dark rounded squares on dark ones. 56px in the set, scaled to 40 or 44 where needed.
